title: GPU driver matrix chaos test report and terraform notes
content:
Purpose:
This is a working-run report of a chaos-style validation pass that combines a driver/CUDA/NCCL compatibility matrix with terraform-driven node pool lifecycle experiments. Goal: identify fragile upgrade permutations we should avoid in customer on-prem + VPC upgrades, and capture terraform module adjustments to reduce blast radius.

High-level summary (TL;DR):
- We ran 72 upgrade permutations across: k8s 1.26/1.27, Nvidia driver 535/545/560, CUDA 12.1/12.2, NCCL 2.18/2.19.
- ~10 permutations had transient failures that resolved with reboot; 6 permutations produced reproducible pod-level GPU allocation errors (failed nvidia-container-runtime handshake or driver API version mismatch).
- Root cause patterns: kernel module reload ordering, dkms vs packaged driver stale modules, and container runtime kubelet config mismatch after driver reinstall.
- Quick mitigations documented below; terraform module notes include a new node-pool lifecycle hook to cordon/drain->reboot->validate-driver->uncordon.

Scope and motivation:
We operate in heterogeneous on-prem environments. Anecdotally customers upgrade k8s or CUDA independently which leads to ambiguous failures. This doc captures reproducible sequences and a recommended safe upgrade recipe and terraform changes to enforce it in automated upgrades.

Environment used for validation:
- Cluster: airgapped lab cluster (k8s 1.26 and 1.27 control planes used across runs)
- Node types: 3x a100-40gb nodes and 3x h100-80gb nodes in separate node pools
- OS: Ubuntu 22.04 (generic onprem images) and RHEL 8.8 (subset runs)
- Container runtime: containerd 1.8.4 with nvidia-container-runtime-hook 1.6.0
- Driver installer variants: packaged .deb (vendor), non-DKMS .run, and dkms-enabled .run
- Monitoring: DCGM exporter + node-exporter, syslogs captured, kernel module probes enabled (modprobe -v logging)
- Automation driver: terraform 1.4.6 + custom module redwood/node_pool (branch test/upgrade-hooks)

Test methodology (chaos-style):
- For each permutation we exercised: node-pool recreate (terraform apply that replaced nodes), in-place driver upgrade (apt/installer), k8s minor/patch bump (control plane simulated in separate clusters), and container rollback (image changes).
- We injected node reboots at two points (before kubelet restart, after driver install), and intentionally delayed kubelet restart to surface kernel module ordering issues.
- Post-change validation: run bench container that allocates GPU with cuda-samples (deviceQuery) and run a small NCCL allreduce loop across 2 pods.

Compatibility matrix (excerpt, textual):
Format: K8S | DRIVER | CUDA | NCCL | NODE-OS | RESULT | NOTES
- 1.26 | 535.86 | 12.1 | 2.18 | ubuntu22.04 | PASS | clean install, dkms driver OK
- 1.26 | 545.65 | 12.2 | 2.18 | ubuntu22.04 | TRANSIENT | required reboot after driver install before kubelet restart
- 1.27 | 560.12 | 12.2 | 2.19 | ubuntu22.04 | FAIL | nvidia-smi reports API mismatch, containerd logs show failed GRPC handshake
- 1.26 | 545.65 | 12.1 | 2.19 | rhel8.8 | PASS-REPRO | worked only when dkms configured; non-dkms failed during kernel update
- 1.27 | 535.86 | 12.1 | 2.18 | ubuntu22.04 | PASS | stable
- 1.27 | 560.12 | 12.2 | 2.19 | rhel8.8 | FAIL | persistent device plugin crashloop
- 1.26 | 545.65 | 12.2 | 2.19 | ubuntu22.04 | TRANSIENT | NCCL sockets raced during container startup, resolved after restart

Observed failure patterns and short analysis:
- Driver API mismatch (nvidia-smi shows lib mismatch)
  - Usually occurs when kernel module version left over from previous driver is still loaded (dkms partial state) while userspace libs replaced. Symptoms: sssd? No, unrelated. Typical log: "Failed to initialize NVML: driver/library version mismatch"
  - Mitigation: ensure module unload and reboot semantics in module; prefer node reboot after driver replace before kubelet restart.

- Container runtime handshake failures
  - containerd/nvidia-container-runtime hook expects libnvidia-container/proxy socket. If kubelet restarts before device plugin rebinds, pod allocation fails. Symptoms: container creation error referencing "failed to get device" and containerd logs show plugin not responding.
  - Mitigation: add kubelet restart ordering - perform driver install -> reboot -> validate /proc/driver/nvidia -> restart kubelet. Add pre-stop hook in device plugin daemonset to wait for module readiness.

- NCCL: networking/syscalls race on pod start
  - Some NCCL versions were sensitive to ephemeral port ranges and host firewall rules during a node rotation. Symptoms: NCCL timeouts during allreduce.
  - Mitigation: enforce iptables rules during upgrade window, ensure DCGM exporter and /etc/hosts consistency on new node images.

Repro steps for a representative FAIL case (1.27 + 560.12 + 12.2 + 2.19):
1) Provision node pool via terraform (test branch)
2) Deploy base driver via apt (560.12) without reboot
3) Restart kubelet only
4) Create test pod with cuda device plugin
5) Observe containerd error: "gpu: failed to allocate" and driver mismatch logs
6) Reboot node -> pods schedule and tests pass (indicates module stale state)

Terraform module notes and recommended changes (actionable):
- node_pool module: add lifecycle hook "post_create_driver_validation" which runs a small userdata script: modprobe -r nvidia || true; apt install -y nvidia-driver-...; sync; reboot; after node returns check /proc/driver/nvidia and run nvidia-smi. Failure -> mark node unhealthy and keep cordoned.
- Add a variable enable_driver_reboot_trigger (default true for onprem) so Dedicated/Hosted can opt out.
- Add null_resource local-exec with retries to run DCGM health probe from control plane to node, gate terraform success on a passing probe.
- Implement graceful rotation submodule: cordon+drain -> disableAutoscaling -> create replacement -> wait for driver probe -> uncordon -> deprovision old. This reduces in-place driver replace failures.
- Add node annotation produced_by_upgrade_run and a terraform output upgrade_run_id to aid forensics and rollback.

Quick checklist for safe on-prem upgrade (candidate playbook):
- Pre-upgrade: capture node-exporter, dmesg, nvidia-smi, kernel version snapshot into artifact store
- For each node pool: cordon and drain with bench pods on other pools to maintain capacity
- Install driver using package channel configured for DKMS where possible or vendor package that includes kernel modules matching OS kernel version
- Reboot node (do not restart kubelet manually before reboot)
- After reboot: confirm /proc/driver/nvidia present, run nvidia-smi, run a smoke NCCL job across at least 2 pods
- If smoke fails -> keep node cordoned, rollback to previous driver (terraform track previous driver package)

Open questions and follow-ups:
- Should we require DKMS in terraform variables for RHEL vs Ubuntu? DKMS reduces some failures but can complicate kernel upgrades.
- How to surface a driver-level preflight to customers with non-root images? We can add a sidecar that runs nvidia-smi in a constrained job and returns health status to the console.
- Can we provide an automated rollback that will restore previous driver and trigger node reboots? Need to store previous driver path in state or artifact store.

Logs & ephemeral artifacts stored:
- s3://lab-artifacts/driver-chaos/run-2025-11-12/ (instrumentation logs, syslogs, dcgm metrics csvs)
- terraform branch: github.com/redwood-inference/terraform-modules@test/upgrade-hooks (PR 78)

Appendix: useful commands observed during runs:
- Check kernel module: lsmod | grep nvidia; cat /proc/driver/nvidia/version
- Force remove module: sudo modprobe -r nvidia_drm nvidia_uvm nvidia_modeset nvidia || true
- Install driver (example): sudo bash NVIDIA-Linux-x86_64-560.12.run --silent --dkms
- Device plugin logs: kubectl -n kube-system logs ds/nvidia-device-plugin-daemonset -c nvidia-device-plugin
- DCGM probe: curl -sS http://NODE:9400/metrics | grep dcgm

Next steps (for eng team):
- Action items assigned:
  - Arjun: add post_create_driver_validation hook and open a follow-up PR for node_pool module (due 2026-02-15)
  - Lena: add terraform tests that gate apply on DCGM probe (PoC) and share perf impact notes (due 2026-02-22)
  - Diego: expand lab runs to RHEL 9.1 and older kernel permutations (due 2026-03-05)
  - Ruth: write an operations KB for customer-facing safe upgrade recipe and include rollback snippets (due 2026-02-28)

Notes to self (raw):
- saw subtle difference between apt packaged driver and .run with --dkms, doc it
- consider adding preflight that warns if kernel headers missing on node images
- run longer NCCL transfer tests (10 minutes) to surface flakiness

End of note.
